_note: MCP wrapper layer for the ade-ops lab. 'databricks' wraps the Databricks workspace API (canonical: databricks-mcp-server from the open-source Databricks AI Dev Kit); 'powerbi' wraps Microsoft's Power BI Modeling MCP (optional, only for /powerbi-* skills). The Databricks profile is referenced by name (e.g. DEMO) and resolved from ~/.databrickscfg. Per-distribution seats may bind to different profiles via their own .mcp.json — that file is gitignored.
_setup: Copy this file to .mcp.json and replace <your-user> with your Windows username. The real .mcp.json is gitignored. The 'powerbi' entry is optional — only needed for /powerbi-model-edit, /powerbi-publish, and TMDL export workflows.
_setup_databricks_prereq: The 'databricks' server requires the Databricks AI dev kit at ~/.ai-dev-kit/ (open-source: https://github.com/databricks-solutions/ai-dev-kit). One-time install on Windows: git clone https://github.com/databricks-solutions/ai-dev-kit "$env:USERPROFILE\.ai-dev-kit\repo" ; cd "$env:USERPROFILE\.ai-dev-kit\repo" ; .\install.ps1 — venv lands at ~/.ai-dev-kit/.venv/ matching the 'databricks' command path below. Also needs a [DEMO] profile in ~/.databrickscfg (referenced via DATABRICKS_CONFIG_PROFILE).
_setup_databricks_auth_pin: The Databricks SDK uses UNIFIED AUTH: if it detects more than one fully-configured method it refuses ('more than one authorization method configured: azure and pat'). On a machine that also carries Azure SP env vars — ARM_CLIENT_ID/ARM_CLIENT_SECRET/ARM_TENANT_ID (Terraform) or AZURE_CLIENT_ID/... — the SDK sees an 'azure' method on top of your PAT profile and breaks. DATABRICKS_CONFIG_PROFILE picks the profile but does NOT pin the method. To immunise the MCP regardless of ambient Azure env vars, add "DATABRICKS_AUTH_TYPE": "pat" to this server's env block alongside the profile.
_setup_powerbi_prereq: The 'powerbi' server wraps Microsoft's official Power BI Modeling MCP — VS Code Marketplace extension 'analysis-services.powerbi-modeling-mcp', distributed as a VSIX (standard ZIP). Manual install: download https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/_apis/public/gallery/publishers/analysis-services/vsextensions/powerbi-modeling-mcp/0.5.7/vspackage?targetPlatform=win32-x64 (latest known 0.5.7 as of 2026-05-21 — see https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=analysis-services.powerbi-modeling-mcp for newer), rename to .zip, extract to C:/MCPServers/PowerBIModelingMCP_x64/. Resulting binary at C:/MCPServers/PowerBIModelingMCP_x64/extension/server/powerbi-modeling-mcp.exe.
_setup_playwright_prereq: The 'playwright' server is used for visual feedback loops on Power BI reports (open report URL, screenshot, iterate). PREREQ: Node.js LTS must be on PATH (`@playwright/mcp` is npx-launched). On Windows: `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS` then restart Claude Code so the updated PATH is inherited. Verify with `node --version` and `npx --version`. Without Node.js the MCP server fails silently — no `mcp__playwright__*` tools in the tool list and no error surfaced. SERVER BINDING: this entry is bound to a DEDICATED Edge profile to keep the operator identity used for screenshots isolated from any Windows-linked accounts (e.g. corporate SSO). On first run the profile is empty; log in once with the identity that has access to the Power BI workspace and the session cookie persists for subsequent screenshot iterations. This entry OVERRIDES any user-level playwright MCP registration on a per-project basis so each seat can bind its own profile.
